text:
incident-bot: AUTO-PAGER fired for stage cluster: deploy redwood-runtime v2.14.0 -> alerts: p95 latency spike (+2.3s), 5xx rate 12% (embed endpoint), affected route: /v1/embeddings (stage-eu). PagerDuty incident created: PD-9812.

jen (oncall): acked. I'm looking. any customer reports? :eyes:

pdmike (product): we saw a handful of API errors from a staging integration test org, but no prod customers. looks like this hit stage-eu only.

raj (sre): initial triage: canary pods are failing readiness on the new quant-path kernel. logs show repeated alloc failures then 502s. attaching small log snippet.

maria (eng): thanks. the change in v2.14.0 enabled "kv-prefetch" + quant-path=p99-squeeze by default for RLHF models. we thought prefetched KV would reduce cold prefix latency but might increase mem pressure.

raj (sre): log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T02:09:12Z redwood-runtime[pid=1345] ERROR kv_cache.cpp:237 OOM while reserving 512MB for kv-cache shard 3
2026-03-14T02:09:12Z redwood-runtime[pid=1345] WARN http: request handler failed status=502 id=fc3a2a
2026-03-14T02:09:13Z redwood-runtime[pid=1345] INFO health: pod terminating for restart
```

jen (oncall): ok that points to mem spike. can we roll the canary back to previous revision while eng investigates? suggest rollback + divert stage-eu traffic to stage-us temporarily.

maria (eng): yes we can rollback. recommended rollback command: 
```
# rollback to revision before v2.14.0
kubectl -n stage rollout undo deploy/redwood-runtime --to-revision=42
```
I also want to push a temporary config patch to disable kv-prefetch: 
```
PATCH configmap/redwood-runtime -p '{"data":{"kv_prefetch":"false"}}'
```

jen (oncall): go ahead with rollback, raj coordinate the kubectl. i'll notify PD and mark customer impact low for now but we'll update.

raj (sre): running rollback now on stage-eu. 
```
kubectl -n stage set image deploy/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=redwood/runtime:v2.13.9
kubectl -n stage rollout status deploy/redwood-runtime --watch
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: PD-9812 acknowledged by jen (oncall). Escalation timer 10m.

maria (eng): if rollback doesn't clear, we should also prepare a model-variant fallback (serve un-quantized checkpoint) and temporary throttle prefetching via runtime flags. prepping a fallback image: redwood/runtime:v2.13.9-unquant.

alex (ops): diverting ingress rules for stage-eu -> stage-us for non-prod traffic. ETA 3m.

raj (sre): rollback finished, pods transitioning. p95 latency back down to baseline in EU stage. 5xx rate dropping to ~0.5%. verifying KV cache sizes now.

pdmike (product): thanks team. can we confirm no persisted user data lost? any request replay side effects?

maria (eng): no persisted state change expected. this was runtime mem pressure causing failures; no DB writes. we'll run a quick verification sweep against staging test org.

jen (oncall): updating PD: incident marked as "mitigated - rollback applied". will keep page open for postmortem and RCA.

incident-bot: PD-9812 status updated: mitigated by jen (oncall). Follow-up owner: alex (ops) for healing and post-rollback warmup.

alex (ops): taking follow-up. I'll run a KV warmup job and keep an eye on evictions and pod OOM trends. creating ticket INC-2901 for follow-up tasks (warmup job, config toggle, postmortem).

raj (sre): quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely memory pressure from kv-prefetch combined with quant-path memory footprint regress on some GPUs; rollout gating insufficient for high-mem paths.

maria (eng): agree. immediate action items: 1) revert default kv-prefetch in next patch, 2) add memory safety checks to canary: p50/p95 mem usage threshold, 3) add a quant-path gradual flag. I'll create PRs.

jen (oncall): handing off to alex for follow-up. I'll be on watch for 30m then clear. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

alex (ops): noted, will file timeline and assign owners. ping me if customers report anything.

pdmike (product): flagging for postmortem agenda: customer impact, rollout checklist update, gating criteria.

incident-bot: thread closed by jen (oncall) for handoff.
